name: Retrofuturism. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics. Provenance: explicit, because the source directly names and describes this visual direction.
visualIdentity: Explicit: choose one historical period's vision of the future and align objects, instruments, interfaces, type, and color to it. Analog controls, early computers, and space-age forms are possible directions. Animation must match the chosen mechanical and display language rather than relying only on neon grids.
suitableUses: Explicit suitability is limited to worlds where a single era's vision of the future defines the whole piece. Inferred suitability includes period-themed explainers, title sequences, and product or editorial visuals. The source gives no formal use-case list, and its suitability for other genres is unspecified.
limitations: Explicit: do not mix incompatible period templates, and do not rely exclusively on neon grids. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics. Stateful simulations must be prepared and cached first. Reference numbers, scenes, and aspect ratios are optional examples, not requirements.
palette: This is an authored example for new artwork, not an approved palette, and the chosen historical period governs. Suggested tokens: background #EEE3CB, foreground #314449, accent_1 #6B9693, accent_2 #BC7751. Task-provided exact colors override these and must be preserved. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 8.027, meeting normal text targets. Accent-to-foreground pairs measure 3.121 and 2.871, so they are decorative only. Recheck composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Motion references are optional. Candidate motion-012 (scroll-driven chaptered scene transition) and motion-015 (scroll-driven storytelling) must be screened against the actual scene, and choosing none is valid. Both need progress-driven, reversible states, with explicit reading holds. Video uses composition time, while live scroll applies only to interactive delivery. Preserve direct seeking and loop seams.
audio: Audio is unspecified by the style, and no fixed music, voice, or sound layer is mandated. The source suggests weighing background music, voiceover, sung vocals, sound effects, ambience, or silence against the topic and motion. Explicit user audio choices and supplied assets take priority. Do not invent audio assets. Verify speech intelligibility, balance, clipping, and picture synchronization.
assetRequirements: The source specifies no fixed asset list. Required inputs include task-provided exact colors and source artwork, which stay unchanged. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering. Authorized audio assets are needed for any sound. Exported tldraw SVG or raster artwork is optional. Any missing assets must be reported, not invented.
combinations: Retrofuturism alone suffices when one era defines the whole world. Suggested hybrid one adds style-075 for operable analog instruments, with switches and dials producing matching on-screen state changes. Suggested hybrid two adds style-009 for mid-century typography and flat background shapes. Hybrids must come from the same era. Avoid mixing 1950s chrome with 1980s neon grids, and avoid purely decorative dials.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation is recorded, and an existing React project alone is insufficient. Three.js and SVG are the recommended style renderers, GSAP is the motion engine, and Motion or PixiJS are optional. chroma.js is optional for contrast checks. Inspect key frames, watch full playback, and verify loops.
